title: Untitled (Surveillance is your busywork)
edition_printrun: Offset lithograph on card, printed in red, black and white. Transit placard for The Public Art Show. Unsigned and unnumbered, no edition size stated.
description:
Untitled (Surveillance is your busywork) is a 1983 transit placard by Barbara Kruger, an offset lithograph on card printed for placement in mass transit.

The horizontal card measures 11 by 28 inches and is printed in red, black and white. A close-cropped black-and-white photograph shows a man's face, his hand holding a dark eyepiece over one eye. The word Surveillance runs in black across a white band at the centre, and "is your busywork" sits in white on a red bar along the bottom edge. The placard was produced in conjunction with The Public Art Show and published by Nexus Press. It is unsigned and was issued without a stated edition size.

Kruger borrows the forms of advertising, graphic design and magazines and speaks directly to the viewer. Here the work takes the format of a transit advertising card and was made to be seen among them.
tags: Art, Barbara Kruger, Conceptual Art, Text Art, Feminism, Pictures Generation, Multiples, Prints, Surveillance, Public Art, Lithograph
notes: Offset lithograph on card printed in red, black and white, 11 x 28 in (27.9 x 71.1 cm), 1983. Unsigned, unnumbered, no edition size stated. Produced as a mass-transit placard in conjunction with The Public Art Show. The publisher is given as Nexus Press, New York, in some listings and as Nexus Contemporary Art Center in others. One bookseller cites The Public Art Show, p. 3, and dates that exhibition 1985, two years after the date given for the placard. An impression is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston (2023.248), catalogued as a colour lithograph, 28 x 71.2 cm.

title: Untitled (Mirror)
edition_printrun: Catalysed-ink three-colour silkscreen on mirrored polished steel. Edition of 120, plus 10 artist's proofs. Numbered, with printed artist stamp.
description:
Untitled (Mirror) is a 2024 edition by Barbara Kruger, a three-colour silkscreen on mirrored polished steel published by Serpentine, London.

The panel measures 600 by 500 mm. A red border frames the mirror surface, and three lines of red capitals run down it: THINKING OF YOU, I MEAN ME, I MEAN YOU. Each YOU is struck through with a black line, and the viewer's reflection fills the space between the words. The work is printed in catalysed ink in an edition of 120 plus 10 artist's proofs, numbered, with a printed artist stamp.

Serpentine released the edition for Barbara Kruger: Thinking of You. I Mean Me. I Mean You., shown at Serpentine South from 1 February to 17 March 2024. The text on the mirror plays on the exhibition's title and offers a further variation on it.

notes: Published by Serpentine, London, on the occasion of Barbara Kruger: Thinking of You. I Mean Me. I Mean You. (Serpentine South, 1 February - 17 March 2024). Catalysed-ink three-colour silkscreen on mirrored polished steel, 600 x 500 mm, edition of 120 plus 10 artist's proofs, numbered, with a printed artist stamp (not hand-signed). The number of this example is not recorded here.

title: Untitled (Kiss), Stool 60
publisher: Artek with the Institute of Contemporary Arts, London
edition_printrun: Artek Stool 60 (design Alvar Aalto) in painted birch and laminate. Edition of 600: an initial run of 300 and a continuation of 300. Hand-numbered, with the artist's stamp on the underside.
description:
Untitled (Kiss) is Barbara Kruger's edition of Alvar Aalto's Stool 60, made by Artek with the Institute of Contemporary Arts, London.

The stool has a round white laminate seat printed with the word KISS in tall black letters, set on three red-painted bent birch legs. It stands 44 cm high with a seat 38 cm across. The ICA dates the work to 2019 and issued it in an initial run of 300 followed by a further 300, for an edition of 600. Each stool is hand-numbered and carries the artist's stamp on the underside, beside Artek's label naming Aalto as designer.

Untitled (Kiss) was the first in a series of artists' versions of Stool 60 commissioned by the ICA and Artek, with a Fischli/Weiss stool announced as the next. Kruger made it in support of the ICA, the first institution to give her a one-person show, in 1983.
tags: Art, Barbara Kruger, Conceptual Art, Text Art, Feminism, Pictures Generation, Multiples, Design, Furniture, Artek, Alvar Aalto
notes: One stool. Commissioned by the Institute of Contemporary Arts, London, and produced by Artek, Helsinki, on Alvar Aalto's Stool 60. The ICA dates the work 2019 and gives the edition as 600 (an initial multiple of 300 and a continuation of 300), each hand-numbered with the artist's stamp on the underside. Examples catalogued by Wright, Chicago, carry decal labels reading 'Artek Made in Finland 2020 / Barbara Kruger' and are dated 2020 there. Materials and dimensions (painted birch, laminate, 17 1/4 in high x 15 in diameter, 44 x 38 cm) follow the Wright catalogue. The number and label date of this example are not recorded here.
